title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 22 Jun to 14 Sep 2026
summary: From 22 Jun to 14 Sep 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 31.35 km2 to 30.17 km2, a change of -3.8%. HH over the land rose by 0.5 dB on average across the 84 days.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake lost 1.18 km2. In HH, 3.21 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.29 km2 darker. HV was steadier, with mean HV moving by 0.02 dB, 0.78 km2 brighter and 0.47 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Rough dry ground and fields had 1.2 km2 brighter in HH, rising 0.46 dB on average. The changing fields type rose 1.23 dB in HV and 1.55 dB in HH. The open water type had 0.73 km2 brighter in HH, and built-up land rose 0.36 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown; the dam's level record would confirm it. Possible cause for the brighter shore: ground left dry by falling water echoes more than water does. Possible cause for the changing fields: crops growing on a few plots; a field visit would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 11.5% and 9.7% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Compare the 1.18 km2 loss with the dam's own level change. Visit the changing fields to learn which crops raise HV in this season.
